title: Zero-Click Search — When Google Answers Instead of Sending Traffic
content:
### **What Changed at the Top of the Page** 

If you have searched for your own company recently, you may have noticed a large summary box above the familiar list of links. That is an AI Overview — a generated answer assembled from multiple sources. 

Industry analyses now put AI Overviews on roughly half of United States search queries, and report that around 58 percent of Google searches end without the user clicking through to any website at all. 

For businesses that built traffic on organic search rankings, that is a meaningful change. Ahrefs reported click reductions of a similar magnitude in early 2026, and several analyses have found traffic declines in the range of 20 to 40 percent for informational queries on sites that have not adapted. 

###  **The Part Most Coverage Gets Wrong** 

It would be easy to read that and conclude local search is finished. The data does not support that conclusion. 

AI Overviews appear far less often on local searches — various analyses put it around 7 percent of local queries, well below the rate for informational searches. And Google reported that Business Profile actions such as calls, directions, and bookings grew 41 percent year over year. 

So the local pack still works. Someone searching for a plumber in their town still sees the map results, and still clicks them. 

###  **What Is Actually Worth Worrying About** 

Two things. First, the trend line is moving toward local rather than away from it, and the share of local searches showing AI answers has been rising each quarter. 

Second, and more immediately: the informational content that many contractors publish to attract homeowners early in their decision — the maintenance guides and how-to articles — is exactly the category being absorbed into AI answers most quickly. 

###  **The Practical Response** 

Keep the Business Profile complete and active, because that is what still drives local clicks and what AI systems cite when they do surface local results. 

And keep at least one channel that does not depend on search results at all. Whatever happens above the fold on a results page has no effect on a conversation at someone's front door.
